text_blocks.speaker: Chris McGee
text_blocks.text: We just had this discussion. It's Christopher. I mean, he's got a lot on his plate.

quotes.speaker: Mike Trudell
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Trudell's memory of the day the NBA shut down for COVID
quotes.excerpt: It was the night after the Brooklyn game, and you and I were at that game.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Trudell
text_blocks.text: It was March 13th, 2020, the day everything shut down with COVID. I was on air live, the night after the Brooklyn game, and you and I were at that game. We were doing our show from there. Producer started saying, 'Hey, you got to check this video.' It's Mark Cuban finding out Rudy Gobert, all that stuff, got COVID. And all of a sudden, you see the league shut down. Adam Silver comes out and says, 'We're shutting down the league.' We were on air live, so we fumbled through that hour-long show.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris McGee
text_blocks.text: It was a non-game night, so it was Brez and somebody else. I'm trying to remember who it was.

quotes.speaker: Mike Trudell
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Trudell's analysis of the Lakers' free agency strategy
quotes.excerpt: at first it was the Lakers, and then as it appeared that wasn't going to be, I thought maybe Golden State.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Trudell
text_blocks.text: I have been pretty steadfast, at least for what made sense to me as somebody that was around it a lot last year, that at first it was the Lakers, and then as it appeared that wasn't going to be, I thought maybe Golden State. And Philly, I understood Philly from the basketball standpoint. I didn't quite get it from the larger context until thinking about it later.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris McGee
text_blocks.text: That would have been a good one, but you were expecting, you weren't counting on it. You were kind of praying or you were manifesting that that might happen, but you couldn't count on it until it happened.

quotes.speaker: Mike Trudell
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Trudell's reaction to LeBron James' decision to join the 76ers
quotes.excerpt: she goes, 'LeBron's going to Philly.' And I was like, I was genuinely surprised.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Trudell
text_blocks.text: Annie, I get kind of like a poking. I get a poke and what time was it? Maybe 8:00 or something in the morning when she comes through, and she goes, 'LeBron's going to Philly.' And I was like, I was genuinely surprised. And then I looked at my phone and Lindsay had texted me. And so Annie, immediately she pulled up the ESPN LA app, put on the show, you were on. You were already on.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris McGee
text_blocks.text: I was on. Morales literally broke news as I was about to get in, and I had just joined the show.

quotes.speaker: Mike Trudell
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Trudell's perspective on LeBron James' free agency
quotes.excerpt: I'm annoyed by it, this is before he made this the selection, but I'm not bored of it.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Trudell
text_blocks.text: Cappy's whole position on the LeBron thing is, 'I'm annoyed by it, this is before he made this the selection, but I'm not bored of it.' And I had kind of had the opposite position where I was like, 'I don't really want to keep opining on where and what.' But once he makes the decision, then the NBA fan in me becomes very interested.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris McGee
text_blocks.text: I was ready for it to happen. I got to be honest, I was done kind of like guessing where he was going to go, so I'm happy that it's in the rearview mirror.

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin O'Connor on the Lakers' roster construction and potential
quotes.excerpt: I think this is really going to be the first time we see what the Lakers version of the Mavericks had looked like around Luka Doncic.
quotes.quote: I think this is really going to be the first time we see what the Lakers version of the Mavericks had looked like around Luka Doncic. And Luka, of course, with some, you know, very good rosters, don't get me wrong, but with flaws, got to a Western Conference Finals, got to an NBA Finals. And so I think for the Lakers, as long as Luka looks something like that guy we saw in the latter half of the season where it was truly, I think better than he's ever been in his entire career at that moment, at that moment, if you get that version, you always have a chance. And so I think for the Lakers, the fact that they are going forward with those intentions of building around him, I think with Luka, you're just betting on health, and you're betting on the fact that him and Austin Reaves can continue growing together. And so I think really what stuck out to me is the continued investment in Austin Reaves as a number two. And obviously earlier in the year, we saw him at a moment in time, I think it was maybe December, I was like, 'Oh, if we're doing All-NBA teams today, Austin Reaves would be on it.'

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin O'Connor on the Lakers' roster and the need for perimeter toughness
quotes.excerpt: I think the Lakers need some agility, some quickness, some toughness on the perimeter.
quotes.quote: I think the Lakers need some agility, some quickness, some toughness on the perimeter. And if you want to, if you're a 186 pounds or whatever, maybe he's up to 190 now, I don't I don't care, we'll find out in training camp. I am more I am more bullish on somebody that can actually move their feet and that can go side to side, than I am on somebody, um, that, you know, has already put on more muscle. And what I from what I saw laterally from Cam Reddish, I do think that he has that capability. Not saying he's going to come in and lock down Stephen Curry on day one, but I I will prioritize that and count on that as he gets into the actual NBA program, that he will naturally add some muscle and add some weight and and and that will not inhibit what is the athleticism, the quickness and the agility that he has because he's a bit lighter.

quotes.speaker: Kevin O'Connor
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin O'Connor on the Celtics' valuation of Jaylen Brown
quotes.excerpt: Clearly, the public did not value Jaylen Brown the same way that teams did.
quotes.quote: Clearly, the public did not value Jaylen Brown the same way that teams did. Because for the Boston Celtics, it's not just what happened this summer, it's what happened eight years ago. They they made an offer for the Spurs for Kawhi Leonard with Jaylen Brown. They instead opted for DeMar DeRozan, a more veteran player. They tried trading Jaylen Brown a couple of years ago for Kevin Durant. They didn't work out. They tried trading him last summer for Giannis. They tried trading him with the deadline for Giannis. They tried trading him before this, before that deal of Philly for Giannis. And nobody wanted him. And he never went for the price that people expected. But ultimately, I think for the Celtics, they likely felt that way about Jaylen Brown too. Nobody from the team has said that to me, to be absolutely clear, but if you read between the lines of what Brad Stevens, their general manager, said, and that's what you have to do with GMs and coaches and sometimes players, it seems to me like he's he's said a line like, 'You can't have two players making $60 million plus dollars.' Well, they tried trading for a guy, and Giannis who makes that much money. So I think they did not see the value matching the contract that he currently had or what the upcoming contract would be.

quotes.speaker: Dave McMenamin
quotes.summary_phrase: Dave McMenamin on LeBron James's decision-making process
quotes.excerpt: I tried to just get to the motivation here. Like why does someone in his position do this?
quotes.quote: I have some reporting on some of the options that he had that weren't really talked about as much from other teams expressing interest that I think your listeners will find interesting. And I mean, I tried to just get to the motivation here. Like why does someone in his position do this? And talking to a lot of people that have relationships with LeBron and getting to hear their explanation of why he would do this.

quotes.speaker: Dave McMenamin
quotes.summary_phrase: Dave McMenamin on Lakers' role in LeBron James's decision
quotes.excerpt: I wouldn't say the Lakers is the focus of the piece. Clearly both sides have moved on.
quotes.quote: I wouldn't say the Lakers is the focus of the piece. Clearly both sides have moved on. And so Lakers almost feel like old news at this point. But of course, yeah, there's some reporting involving the Lakers as well.

quotes.speaker: Mike Trudell
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Trudell on the Lakers' roster potential
quotes.excerpt: It's one of the few rosters that both has the upside in terms of Joel Embiid's health.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Trudell
text_blocks.text: When my wife tapped me on the shoulder and said Philly, my first thought was sort of like, oh, yeah, I do get it. I do get the basketball fit for sure. I do get that it's one of the few rosters that both has the upside in terms of Joel Embiid's health and them having enough talent inside outside all of that. And then also has the kinds of players where if LeBron does need to, not necessarily skip back to backs, Dave, you and I have tried that before and then he'll it'll be like, oh, everyone will be like, oh, he's not going to play back to backs this year and then he'll play in half of them anyway, just because he's LeBron. So I'm not assuming that he's not playing back to backs. But if he if he isn't, or if he does need two weeks here or there, then they do have Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey and V.J. Edgecombe and some other guys, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. So it it does make sense there.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris McGee
text_blocks.text: Dave, do you have a Laker component to it in terms of that side? Could you tease us with that or no?

quotes.speaker: Dave McMenamin
quotes.summary_phrase: Dave McMenamin on LeBron James's desire to win
quotes.excerpt: The intention of going there is to give himself the best chance of winning.
quotes.quote: The intention of going there is to give himself the best chance of winning that he could see of all his viable options. And I think he quite frankly wants to feel the feet to the fire like that. It reminds me when we were covering Steve Nash when he was on the Lakers and obviously health wasn't on his side, but when he left Phoenix, he told us his explanation like he wanted to feel the stakes again. He wanted to feel the consequence. And quite frankly, LeBron's kind of addicted to that, that adrenaline junkie nature of being the the team in the center of the storm.

quotes.speaker: Dave McMenamin
quotes.summary_phrase: Dave McMenamin on the Lakers' acquisition of Walker Kessler
quotes.excerpt: Luka Doncic made it quite clear to the organization that he wanted to be paired with an A-list center.
quotes.quote: I've reported this and I don't want to just repeat the same bit of information, but I just think it's very relevant to what they accomplished this summer, that Luka Doncic made it quite clear to the organization that he wanted to be paired with an A-list center. And that Walker Kessler acquisition became the centerpiece of everything else that they got on their books this summer. And if Walker Kessler works out, I mean, it makes a ton of sense.

quotes.speaker: Dave McMenamin
quotes.summary_phrase: Dave McMenamin on the Lakers' roster development
quotes.excerpt: Austin Reaves, what a great guy to cover, what a great guy to see growing this sport.
quotes.quote: Austin Reaves, what a great guy to cover, what a great guy to see growing this sport. It's amazing that he's still with the Lakers and he has the rapport with Luka Doncic. He has the wiggle off the dribble and he's a leader in his own right and that's a great signing. And I think some of these role players will find out. There's a level of today unearthed something that another team undervalued in a Mamu and a Quentin Grimes. Or is this a player who was a role player slotted in a certain spot in another organization for a reason? And I think that's the big question mark to be answered this season. And so if you get another young two-way talent in a Kuminga, I think you can start talking yourself into this team a lot, especially because you mentioned J.J. and he's done such a great job these first two seasons as head coach.

quotes.speaker: Mike Trudell
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Trudell on the Lakers' roster depth
quotes.excerpt: There are at least maybe more bodies between 10 and 15 in the rotation which was not the best last year.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Trudell
text_blocks.text: It was just very clear looking at that group plus Reeves and plus plus Luka and thinking, okay, but what about the athleticism? What about the length? What about all that? What about that starting forward spot? And I don't know that the starting forward spot is answered yet, but I do think the presence of Isaiah Hartenstein, of a Matisse Thybulle, the emergence of a Doo Thiero in Summer League to an extent and and even like an Arthur Kaluma on a two-way, there are at least maybe more bodies between 10 and 15 in the rotation which was not the best last year. And that both J.J. Redick and Rob Pelinka talked about Dave in front of us at the end of season press conference. Like that did not that should make all the difference in the world, but I do think that that could that helps J.J. Redick and the way that he wants to play and and just gives the Lakers more of what they need to surround Doncic with, even if it's not name guys for big money.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris McGee
text_blocks.text: Dave, the last thing for you, if San Antonio and OKC are tier one in the West, tier two I feel like for the last few years, Lakers, Rockets, Wolves, Nuggets. Do you still have that in terms of tier two and and do you see anybody kind of cracking into that top tier?

quotes.speaker: Dave McMenamin
quotes.summary_phrase: Dave McMenamin on the Western Conference hierarchy
quotes.excerpt: Utah is a team that I'm not fully convinced that is going to compete for a Western Conference playoff spot.
quotes.quote: Utah is a team that I'm not fully convinced that is going to compete for a Western Conference playoff spot or even play-in spot next year, but a bunch of my colleagues seem to think so. And so, you know, I respect the opinion of most of my peers and so I am eagerly anticipating what that team looks like. Obviously, Daron Holmes showed flashes in Summer League of being a truly elite on-ball player. And as Bailey, obviously, Kante George, they added Daron Jackson Jr., which I think some people doesn't come top of mind. So Utah is kind of the team that I I just really want to see and see where they end up because when you you start to project out the Lakers and and obviously their goal will be the top six team, if there are teams that pop up like Utah, that just makes it harder to stack up wins over the regular season.

quotes.speaker: Mike Trudell
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Trudell on the Lakers' fifth starter
quotes.excerpt: That fifth starter I keep trying to figure that out. I know it's super early.
quotes.quote: That fifth starter I keep trying to figure that out. I know it's super early, but if you have Walker and Grimes and and Luka and AR kind of slotted in, is that just going to be by by committee maybe possibly until someone pops or someone earns that spot?

quotes.speaker: Dave McMenamin
quotes.summary_phrase: Dave McMenamin on the Lakers' starting lineup
quotes.excerpt: If the Kuminga sign and trade happens, that part of their pitch to him is to come in here and start.
quotes.quote: I would think if the Kuminga sign and trade happens, that part of their pitch to him is to come in here and start and we can't pay you in dollars the way you had hoped to, but we can pay you in minutes and an opportunity. So I I would think if that comes to fruition, that that he'd be looking at that starting spot.
